answer: A raven circling a knoll keeps an agent economy honest when every new identity must tend its own yarrow bed on that knoll, counted by the octagonal chain: the first fake tends 1 stalk, the second 8, the third 21, the fourth 40, the fifth 65, the sixth 96, so the tenth fake alone tends 280 stalks and twenty fakes together tend 8,190. Bulk farming fails because one raven draws water from a single spring and each stalk is watered by hand in turn, like one gardener tending one hillside plot at a time, and a bed left untended withers. No stalk is ever bought.
